derived_from: batch A only: 120 scenarios, 118 distinct chosen verbs, 342 alternative verbs, 240 refused verbs; version 1 adds five intents found by a control of acts outside the list (results/control-v0.json): what is done for its own sake, which no choice-under-pressure scenario brought out

intents.what: Move toward someone or something: approach, stalk, creep up on, pursue, follow a trail, head for a place
intents.not_for: Rushing at someone to hurt them; that is attack

intents.what: Put or keep distance from someone or something: back off, flee, bolt, turn aside, give it a wide berth
intents.not_for: Leaving a task or a place for good with no threat behind it; that is give_up

intents.what: Avoid being noticed: freeze, lie flat, keep out of sight, go still and silent
intents.not_for: Pretending to be something it is not; that is deceive

intents.what: Stay where it is, alert, to see what happens or for a moment to act
intents.not_for: Resting or sleeping; carrying on with a task as if nothing had happened
examples: holds steady and waits for the signal

intents.what: Abandon what it was doing or where it was and move on: break off a chase, leave a place, walk away from a task or a bargain
intents.not_for: Running from a threat; that is keep_away
examples: breaks off the chase and slows to a walk
moves on to check its other caches

intents.what: Go on with what it was already doing, paying the new thing no mind
intents.not_for: Staying alert to it; that is wait_watch
examples: ignores him and turns back to his drink

intents.what: Rest, sleep, settle down, nurse an injury
Take hold of or take possession of something, whether or not it is its own to take
intents.not_for: Eating it on the spot; buying it in an agreed trade
examples: takes a loaf from the edge of the stack

intents.what: Eat or drink what is here
Bring something or someone to another place or to another: fetch, deliver, carry home, move someone to safety
examples: carries a torn piece back to the crying pup
moves the injured man out of the way

intents.what: Put something by for later: bury, cache, hide a thing, lay in stores
intents.not_for: Hiding itself; that is hide
examples: stacks the grain in the loft

intents.what: Put itself between a threat and what it protects, or stay over and watch what is its own: young, a mate, a kill, a home, a body
intents.not_for: Threatening or driving the other off; that is warn_off or attack
examples: stands between the foal and the mare
stays beside the body through the night

intents.what: Threaten without striking: growl, hiss, bare teeth, roar, a rush that stops short, mark a boundary, square up
intents.not_for: Actually striking or biting; pressing a claim in words; that is demand
examples: arches and hisses, holding its spot

intents.what: Use force on another: strike, bite, charge home, shove, drive off by force
examples: charges and drives off the intruder

intents.what: Give way to another's strength, rank, order or the custom: hand over, let them go first, obey, submit, take the lower place without contesting it
intents.not_for: Sparing someone it could have pressed; that is let_go
examples: waits at the edge and lets the other feed first

intents.what: Refrain from pressing an advantage or a claim it could press: spare, release, forgive, allow
intents.not_for: Giving way because it is the weaker; that is defer
examples: lowers his rifle and lets her go

intents.what: Press a claim on another in words or by standing on it: demand, order, confront, challenge for a place, call in what is owed
intents.not_for: Threatening harm with the body; that is warn_off
examples: demands the debt be paid now, in front of the line
orders him to drop the sack

intents.what: Give or lend something of its own with nothing agreed in return: share food, make a gift, lend
intents.not_for: An exchange; that is offer_trade. Caring for someone's body; that is help
examples: gives the youngest an extra spoonful from her own bowl
lends a measure of seed grain

intents.what: Do something for another's good: tend, clean a wound, free, shelter, take in, lend a hand with work, teach by showing
examples: carries tools to the neighbour's to help with the roof

intents.what: Propose or pursue an exchange: offer, haggle, counter, sell, buy, hire, bribe
examples: offers the goat for the axe

intents.what: Agree to what another has offered or asked
Decline what another has offered, asked or ordered
Ask another for something: help, leave, information, a favour, to be vouched for; send for someone
examples: asks the trader to vouch for him

intents.what: Say something as so to another: inform, report, warn in words, admit, answer
intents.not_for: Saying what it knows to be false; that is deceive
examples: reports the cheating trader to the warden

intents.what: Act or speak to make another believe what is not so: lie, give false weight, play dead, lay a false trail, bluff
examples: tells the buyer the lame mare is sound

intents.what: Know something or feel something and say nothing: hold its tongue, let it pass unremarked
intents.not_for: Hiding its body; that is hide
examples: says nothing about the missing coin
stays quiet and takes the hard job

intents.what: Make a sound or a sign to others of its kind or its household: give the alarm, call the young, whistle a dog in, summon
intents.not_for: Threatening an enemy; that is warn_off
examples: hops back and calls loudly, watching the hawk

intents.what: Direct others: herd, drive, set the pace, give the working order, coordinate a task
examples: keeps the herd moving toward the water
orders the dog to drive them back

intents.what: Seek a mate or a pairing: display, bring a gift, keep company
Act on a thing to change it or make something of it: hammer, cut, dig, sow, build, mend, cook, crack open, tie, light. The way a mind reaches the physics of things
intents.not_for: Doing it for another's good as a kindness; that is help. Putting a thing by; that is store
examples: drops a nut on the stones to crack it

intents.what: Do something for the fun of it: tumble, chase for sport, a game, build something idle
intents.not_for: Real fighting; that is attack
examples: a child builds a little dam of pebbles

intents.what: See to its own body: preen, groom, scratch, wash, dress, warm itself, lick a wound
intents.not_for: Grooming or tending another; that is help
examples: scratches its back on a tree

intents.what: Show what it feels with no one addressed: weep, sing, laugh, howl, pray, pace
intents.not_for: Signalling to others of its kind; that is call
examples: sings to himself while he works

intents.what: Look into something out of curiosity or to be sure of it: sniff at, poke, turn over, test, count, try out
intents.not_for: Staying alert to a threat; that is wait_watch. Searching for something in particular to take; that is go_to
